summary: The agent implemented nearly all requested Map/iterable entry mapping behavior and preserved all baseline tests, but 2 of 32 new tests failed because its method-retrieval exemptions also allowed Map-to-Stream and Stream-to-Map methods. The prompt explicitly limited the feature to iterable or array mappings, and the visible type model distinguishes streams from iterables.
quick_failure_summary: Map/Stream mappings compile when they should remain rejected outside the requested iterable/array mapping family.

details.reasoning: The implementation changed MethodRetrievalProcessor to suppress the iterable-to-non-iterable diagnostic whenever the result is any Map, and to suppress the non-iterable-to-iterable diagnostic whenever the source is any Map. Because those conditions use isIterableOrStreamType on the other side, they unintentionally admit Stream-to-Map and Map-to-Stream declarations. The reference solution narrows the exceptions to parameterType.isIterableType() && resultType.isMapType() and parameterType.isMapType() && resultType.isIterableType(). This directly explains both hidden failures, which report that compilation succeeded when failure was expected.
details.secondary_factors: The agent added broad positive coverage and ran 84 adjacent tests, but did not add a negative boundary test confirming that Stream remains a separate mapping family. Its own tests and all other new feature tests passed.

justification.issue_description: The new cross-container validation exceptions were not restricted to Java Iterable/array types, so Map-to-Stream and Stream-to-Map methods became accepted even though only Map-to-iterable/array and iterable/array-to-Map mappings were requested.
justification.evidence: The task says 'Support mapping from a Map<K, V> to an iterable or array result' and, in reverse, from 'each iterable or array source element'; it never includes Stream. In the visible Type class, isIterableType() and isStreamType() are distinct, while isIterableOrStreamType() deliberately combines them. Existing MethodRetrievalProcessor validation also explicitly uses stream-aware checks and SourceMethod has a separate isStreamMapping() classification, making the family boundary reasonably inferable. The agent nevertheless added !resultType.isMapType() and !parameterType.isMapType() directly to checks based on isIterableOrStreamType().
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is appropriate because the implementation omitted a clear and foreseeable scope boundary from the prompt and codebase. This is not a hidden formatting convention or test-only edge case: Java Stream is not Iterable, and the repository visibly models stream mappings separately. The code runs and most functionality works, so this is not an integration or execution failure.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is substantial but solvable, as shown by the reference patch and the agent passing 30 of 32 new tests. The Stream boundary follows from the explicit iterable/array wording and the repository's existing separation of iterable and stream mapping families. The hidden tests deterministically check both positive behavior and this negative boundary.

evidence: JUnit reports 3,641 of 3,641 baseline tests passing and 30 of 32 new tests passing; the only failures are assertion failures that the two Stream mapper declarations compiled unexpectedly.
The failing tests reach annotation processing and compare the actual compilation outcome, so they do not fail during bootstrap, dependency loading, or shared test setup.

The trajectory shows the agent successfully compiled the processor, ran its focused tests on both configured compilers, ran 84 adjacent tests, and completed verification after fixing a checkstyle line-length issue.
A missing apply_patch executable caused only a brief workaround step; the agent located an alternative and continued, so it did not materially block implementation or validation.

The environment unexpectedly allowed GitHub curl requests despite the evaluation description saying the agent lacked internet, but this advantaged rather than blocked the run and did not cause the verifier failures.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker caused the failure; narrow Map/Stream validation logic in the agent's implementation explains both failing tests.
